photos.title: United States Capitol - west front
photos.what: The west front of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., under a blue sky: the dome in the middle, the Senate wing on the left and the House wing on the right, a lawn and flower beds in front. A few people far away on the paths and steps, too small to recognize.
photos.caption: The United States Capitol from the west. The Senate meets in the wing on the left, and the House in the wing on the right.
photos.alt: The west front of the United States Capitol in Washington, with the dome in the middle, the Senate wing on the left and the House wing on the right
photos.author: Architect of the Capitol
photos.credit: Photo: Architect of the Capitol, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
photos.provenance: Photo by the Architect of the Capitol, 1997 (aoc.gov photo gallery, 72350_hr_1997.jpg), a work of the U.S. federal government. Commons file page read 2026-11-04: Author 'Architect of the Capitol', Permission {{PD-USGov-Congress-AOC}}, Date 1997, 3000 x 1556. Commons image notes on the file mark the Senate chamber in the left (north) wing and the House chamber in the right (south) wing. Downloaded as the Commons original on 2026-11-04. Licence also checked by the batch verifier (VERIFY.md, photos table).
photos.license_note: Commons: PD-USGov-Congress-AOC, a work of the Architect of the Capitol, an agency of the U.S. legislative branch, in the public domain.
photos.subject_check: Looked at full size (1920 px) by the writer of /buyers/flood-insurance-after-the-election/ on 2026-11-04: the building is the subject. People on the paths and steps are a few pixels tall and cannot be recognized. The Statue of Freedom on the dome is small and in the background. No logo, sign or plate.

photos.title: Florence Inundates the Carolinas: rain accumulation, Sept. 13-16, 2018
photos.what: A NASA satellite map of North and South Carolina. Colors show estimated rain from Hurricane Florence from Sept. 13 to 16, 2018: red and orange over southeastern North Carolina near the landfall, yellow and green along the coast at the state line, blue farther inland. A dotted line in the ocean shows the storm's track to the coast. No labels, no people.
photos.caption: Rain from Hurricane Florence, Sept. 13 to 16, 2018, estimated by NASA satellites. Red marks the most rain. The dotted line is the storm's track to the coast.
photos.alt: NASA satellite map of rain from Hurricane Florence over North and South Carolina, heaviest in red over southeastern North Carolina, with the storm's track shown as a dotted line

place.sublocation: The Carolinas coast, including Horry County

photos.author: NASA Earth Observatory (Joshua Stevens and Lauren Dauphin)
photos.credit: Map: NASA Earth Observatory (Joshua Stevens and Lauren Dauphin), public domain.
photos.provenance: From NASA Earth Observatory image record 92775, 'Florence Inundates the Carolinas' (file carolinas_mrg_2018259_lrg.png, 3110 x 1622, downloaded from assets.science.nasa.gov on 2026-11-04). NASA's text: 'The right image shows the rain accumulation from September 13-16. These rainfall data are remotely-sensed estimates that come from the Integrated Multi-Satellite Retrievals (IMERG)'. The same record's soil moisture image (carolinas_smp_2018254) is on Wikimedia Commons with {{PD-USGov-NASA}} and was licence-checked by the batch verifier (VERIFY.md); this rainfall image is its companion in the same NASA record, by the same authors, under the same NASA public domain terms. Commons rate-limited the download (HTTP 429), so the file came from NASA directly.
photos.license_note: A work of NASA, a U.S. federal agency, made as part of its official duties: public domain (Commons template PD-USGov-NASA, used on the companion file in the same record).
